summary: The root زبد primarily refers to fresh butter, churned from milk. It can also metaphorically describe the "cream" or best part of something, like discourse.
lane: زُبْدٌ ذ [ Fresh butter of the cow or buffalo or sheep or goat; ] what is produced by churning from milk (Mgh, Msb) of cows [or buffaloes ] and of sheep or goats; what is thus produced from camels' milk being termed جُبَابٌ , not زُبْدٌ ; (Msb;) the زُبْد of سَمْن before it is clarified over the fire; (L;) [i. e. butter before it is clarified over the fire; ] the زُبْد [in the CK, erroneously, زَبَد ] of milk; (S, K;) what is extracted from milk; (M;) and signifies the same as زُبْدٌ : (K:) is a more particular term, (S, M, L, Msb,) meaning a piece, bit, portion, or somewhat, of زُبْد : (L:) and زُبْدُ اللَّبَنِ signifies also the froth ( رَغْوَة ) of milk [if this be not a mistake occasioned by finding الزُّبْدُ expl. as meaning زَبَدُ اللَّبَنِ instead of زُبْدُ اللَّبَنِ ]. (L.) قَدْ صَرَّحَ المَحْضُ عَنِ الزُّبْدِ [ The clear milk has become distinct from the fresh butter ] is a prov., relating to the appearance of the truth after information that has been doubted. (L.) And اِرْتَجَنَتِ is another prov. [expl. in art. رجن ]. (L.) -b2- has for its pl. زُبَدٌ , which is metonymically applied to (tropical:) The choice, or best, portions, [or what we often term the cream (by which word the sing. also may be rendered) of anything; as, for instance,] of discourse, or of a story or the like. (Har p. 222, q. v.) -b3- [And it also means (assumed tropical:) An issue, or event: (see an ex. voce مَخَضَ :) generally, such as is relishable, or pleasing. Hence, app.,] one says, كَانَ لِقَاؤُكَ العُمُرِ (tropical:) [ The meeting with thee was emphatically the event of life; meaning, the most relishable, or pleasing, event of life ]. (A, TA.)

headwords.def: (As, S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. زَبُدَ, (As, S, A, Msb,) inf. n. زَبْدٌ, (As, Msb,) He fed him with, or gave him to eat, زُبْد [i. e. fresh butter ]. (As, S, A, Mgh, Msb, K.) And hence, (Mgh,) زَبَدَهُ, (As, S, A, Mgh, Msb,) or زَبَدَ لَهُ, (K, [app. a mistranscription, for its aor. is there mentioned immediately after without the prep.,]) aor.

زبّد شِدْقُهُ , (S, K,) inf. n. تَزْبِيدٌ; (K;) and; both signify the same [i. e. The side of his mouth had froth, or foam, appearing upon it; like زَبَّبَ and تَزَبَّبَ ]: (S, K:) and said of a man, [like تَزَبَّبَ,] He being angry, froth, or foam, appeared upon each corner of his mouth. (TA.) See also 4, in two places. زَبَّدَتِ القُطْنَ, (A, L,) inf. n.
فُلَانٌ يُزَابِدُ فُلَانًا (tropical:) Such a one speaks in like manner as does such a one. (A, TA.)

(S, A, Msb, K,) inf. n. إِزْبَادٌ, (Msb,) said of wine, or beverage, (S,) or of the sea, (A, Msb, K,) &c., (Msb,) or of the sea when in a state of commotion, (S, * A,) and of a cookingpot, and of the mouth of a braying camel, (A,) [&c., see زَبَدٌ,] It frothed, or foamed, or cast forth froth or foam: (S, * A, Msb, K:) and [in like manner], inf. n. تَزْبِيدٌ, said of milk, it [ frothed, or foamed; or] had froth, or foam, upon it.

تَزَبَّدَ see 1: and see also 2, in two places. تزبّدهُ (assumed tropical:) He swallowed it (K) like as one swallows a piece of fresh butter: (TA:) or he took the clear, or pure, or choice, part of it. (K, TA.) Of anything of which the clear, or pure, or choice part has been taken, one says, تُزُبِّدَ. (TA.) [Hence,] تزبّد اليَمِينَ (assumed tropical:) He took the oath hastily; was hasty in taking it.

[originally an inf. n.,] (tropical:) A gift. (S, A, Mgh, Msb.) So in the saying (S, TA) of Mo- hammad, (TA,) mentioned in a trad., إِنَّا لَا نَقْبَلُ زَبْدَ المُشْرِكِينَ (tropical:) [ Verily we will not accept the gift of the believers in a plurality of Gods ]. (S, TA.) And so in the saying, نَهَى عَنْ زَبْدِ المُشْرِكِينَ (tropical:) (A, Mgh, Msb) i. e. [ He (Mohammad) forbade ] the acceptance of the gift [ of the believers in a plurality of Gods ]. (Msb.)

[ Fresh butter of the cow or buffalo or sheep or goat; ] what is produced by churning from milk (Mgh, Msb) of cows [or buffaloes ] and of sheep or goats; what is thus produced from camels' milk being termed جُبَابٌ, not زُبْدٌ; (Msb;) the زُبْد of سَمْن before it is clarified over the fire; (L;) [i. e.

Froth, foam, spume, or scum: (L:) it is of water, (S, L, K,) &c.; (K;) of the sea, (A, Msb,) &c., like رَغْوَةٌ [ in signification ]; (Msb;) and of a cooking-pot; (A;) and of a camel, (S,) [i. e.] of a braying camel's mouth, (A,) or the white foam upon the lips of a camel when he is excited by lust; (TA;) and of the cud; and of spittle; (L;) and [the scum, or dross, ] of silver: (S:) is a more particular term [meaning a portion, or somewhat, thereof ]: (S:) the pl.
[ Butyraceous: a rel. n. from زُبْدٌ ]. See خَشْخَاشٌ.

[ Civet; ] a certain perfume, well known: the lawyers and the lexicologists err in saying that it is a certain beast, [meaning the civet-cat, ] from which the perfume is milked: (K:) or this assertion is not to be reckoned as a mistake, the word being tropically thus applied: so says El- Karáfee: and Z and other authors worthy of confidence thus apply it [as a coll. gen. n.]: Z also mentions a saying in which is applied [as a n.
like غُرَابٌ [in measure], Fresh butter ( زُبْد ) that has become bad, or spoiled, in the churning: or, as some say, thin milk. (TA voce اِخْتَلَطَ, q. v.) [See also زُبَّادُ اللَّبَن, below.]

زُبَّادُ اللَّبَنِ [ The watery part of milk; ] that [ part ] in which is no good, of milk. (S, K. [See also زُبَادٌ.]) It is said in a prov., اِخْتَلَطَ الخَاثِرُ بِالزُّبَّادِ (S) [ The thick milk became mixed with the thin watery part: or] (tropical:) the good became mixed with the bad: relating to a case of difficulty, and applied to the mixture of truth with falsehood. (L. [See Freytag's Arab. Prov., i. 434: and see اِخْتَلَطَ.]) See also زُبْدٌ.
Possessing, or a possessor of, زُبْد [or fresh butter ]; (L;) as also. (K.)
بَحْرٌ مُزْبِدٌ [ A frothing, or foaming, sea; or] a tumultuous, frothing, or foaming, sea. (S, A.) [Hence,] أَبْيَضُ مُزْبِدٌ (tropical:) Intensely white. (A, TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
